title: Surely God Is Good to Israel

reflections.title: "I Was a Brute Beast"

reflect.text: In Psalm 73:22, the psalmist honestly admits his foolishness before God. He had looked at the easy lives of the wicked and felt envy. This was not just a small mistake; it was a sinful attitude that forgot where the ungodly would ultimately end up. We act with pride if we think we are immune to such thoughts or that we are wiser than the psalmist.

We often fall into the very same trap. In difficult and dark times, we easily misjudge what God is doing in our lives. We might complain that everything is against us, failing to realize that God uses trials for our lasting good. As Charles Spurgeon reminds us, our hearts are prone to "a sinful folly." When we recognize our own spiritual ignorance, we stop trusting our own limited thinking. Instead, we learn to rely completely on God's wise guidance each day.

questions: Have you ever envied someone who does not follow God?
How can admitting your own lack of wisdom help you trust God's plan instead?
reflections.prayer: Lord, forgive us when we envy others or doubt Your goodness during hard times. We confess that our own understanding is limited and easily led astray. Teach us to lean completely on Your wisdom rather than our own thoughts. Amen.

reflections.title: "You Hold My Right Hand"

reflect.text: Even when unanswered prayer or deep sorrow turns into bitterness, God does not leave us. The psalmist had just confessed how senseless he had been, yet he realized something wonderful: he was still constantly with God. The Lord holds our right hand and never looks away. Because of God's kindness and grace, our failures do not remove us from His presence. As Charles Spurgeon explains, God's eye "never sleepeth, but is perpetually watching over my welfare."

God does not simply keep us safe; He also leads us every step of the way. We do not have to guess our path through life, because He directs us through the trustworthy counsel of the Bible. Like a blind man holding the arm of a faithful friend, we can depend on His wisdom instead of our own frail judgment.

Best of all, this earthly journey has a certain destination. When our days here come to an end, God will welcome us into glory. We will not arrive in heaven as strangers, for our loving Father will receive us home forever. This glorious hope gives us peace through every present grief.

questions: How does knowing that God continually holds your hand comfort you when you feel weak?
How does the promise of being welcomed into glory change the way you face today's troubles?
reflections.prayer: Father, thank You for holding our hand, even when our faith wavers and our hearts grow weary. Guide our daily steps through the truth of Your Word. Keep our eyes fixed on the eternal home You have prepared for us. Amen.

D8.author: Scott Hubbard
D8.work: The Beast I Become: How to Bring Bitterness to God

reflections.title: Surely God Is Good

reflect.text: It can be deeply unsettling to watch proud and corrupt people enjoy comfortable, healthy lives while faithful believers suffer sickness, exhaustion, or grief. Asaph was completely honest about how close he came to slipping. He even wondered whether keeping his heart clean had been entirely pointless. When we look only through our earthly senses, we easily question God's kindness and justice.

The turning point came when Asaph entered God's sanctuary. Being in God's presence changed how he saw everything. He realized that the ease of the wicked is fragile and will end in sudden ruin. Instead of judging God by our difficult circumstances, we must learn to view our circumstances through God. Even when our physical bodies and hearts fail us, God Himself remains our everlasting portion and strength.

In the end, what matters most is not having an easy life on earth, but having unbroken fellowship with God. While those far from Him will perish, those who draw near to Him find a true refuge. When we surrender our weakness to Him, we can face each day with courage and boldly declare all that He has done.

questions: When life seems unfair, how can looking at your circumstances from God's point of view help your heart?
In what area of physical or emotional weakness do you need God to be your strength today?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, You are good, even when the world around us seems confusing and unfair. When our own strength is gone, be the firm rock of our hearts. Draw us near to You and help us tell others of Your faithfulness. Amen.
